{{Quote|When Kathy Kennedy brought me on board to make a ''Star Wars'' movie, her central mandate to me was 'I want a Shawn Levy movie. I want a story and a tone that reflects you and your taste and what you bring to your movies — with a ''Star Wars'' story.' So I have felt extremely empowered.|Shawn Levy discusses his ''Star Wars'' project|<ref name="Variety" />}}
'''''Star Wars: Starfighter''''' is a stand-alone live-action film currently in post-production at [[Lucasfilm]] with filmmaker [[Shawn Levy]] serving as the director and Lucasfilm president [[Kathleen Kennedy]] producing the project. The film is set to take place around five [[Standard year|years]] after the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']], and may include characters from the [[sequel trilogy]]. [[Ryan Gosling]] will star in the film.

==Plot summary==
{{Quote|Shawn's is a standalone ''Star Wars'' story that’ll take place post-nine, maybe five or six years out.|Kathleen Kennedy, to Deadline|<ref name="KK Q&A" />}}
[[Shawn Levy]]'s ''Star Wars'' film is set to take place around five [[Standard year|years]] following the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']], and according to [[Lucasfilm]] president [[Kathleen Kennedy]], may include [[sequel trilogy]] characters.<ref name="KK Q&A" />

==Development==
===Early beginnings===
{{Quote|I really wanted to craft something that felt organic to me, both in tone and characters, so I think that there is — there is certainly the Force and a connection to something bigger than our individual selves. And the way that that can make us powerful, those themes, combined with visual delight and wish fulfillment, that's ''Star Wars'' to me.|Shawn Levy, on his film|<ref name="Collider">{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/shawn-levy-star-wars-update|text=Shawn Levy Jumps to Hyperspace With an Update on His 'Star Wars' Film|authpr=Justin Klawans|date=2014-08-07|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|''Collider'']]|archivedate=20240810135349}}</ref>}}
In a [[2026]] interview, Lucasfilm President [[Kathleen Kennedy]] revealed that she had first approached Levy about a ''Star Wars'' project before of the [[Netflix]] series ''[[Wikipedia:Stranger Things|Stranger Things]]'' erupted in popularity, which took up much of his time.<ref name="Deadline Kennedy">{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2026/01/kathleen-kennedy-exit-interview-1236665253|text=A Shift In The Force For Lucasfilm’s Kathleen Kennedy: The Exit Interview|author=Mike Flemming Jr.|date=2026-01-15|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20260115233219}}</ref> ''Stranger Things'' first debuted on 	[[July 15]], [[2016]], and became a surprise hit, transforming Netflix.<ref name="STRelease">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/there-will-never-be-another-show-like-stranger-things|text=There Will Never Be Another Show Like Stranger Things|author=Alex Zalben|date=2026-01-02|work=IGN|archivedate=20260107215559}}</ref>

Years later, it was reported by [[Wikipedia:Deadline|''Deadline]] on [[November 8]], [[2022]] that Levy would direct a ''Star Wars'' film after the completion of the [[Wikipedia:Marvel Cinematic Universe|Marvel Cinematic Universe]] film [[Wikipedia:Deadpool & Wolverine|''Deadpool & Wolverine'']] and the [[Wikipedia:Stranger Things season 5|fifth season]] of ''Stranger Things''.<ref name="Deadline">{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2022/11/star-wars-film-shawn-levy-directing-talks-after-deadpool-3-stranger-things-lucasfilm-1235166644|text=Shawn Levy In Talks To Direct A 'Star Wars' Film After 'Deadpool 3' & 'Stranger Things' Final Eps|author=Mike Fleming Jr, Justin Kroll|date=2022-11-08|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20240604221118}}</ref> Levy publicly confirmed the report the same day on [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]].<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|username=ShawnLevyDirect|url=status/1590045939087323137|name=[[Shawn Levy]]|date=2022-11-08|quote=Childhood me is losing his shit right now. Grown-up me is too. @DEADLINE|archivedate=20231123053707}}</ref> On [[October 23]], [[2023]], [[Shawn Levy]] was interviewed by [[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']] on his projects and briefly spoke on his film, stating that [[Lucasfilm]] President [[Kathleen Kennedy]] wanted a ''[[Star Wars]]'' film with a story and tone that reflects Levy and his taste. With the [[2024]] [[Wikipedia:Marvel Cinematic Universe|Marvel Cinematic Universe]] film [[Wikipedia:Deadpool & Wolverine|''Deadpool & Wolverine'']]{{'s}} positive production, Levy stated to ''Variety'' that he felt a similar optimism going into the development of his ''Star Wars'' film.<ref name="Variety" /> ''Starfighter'' was envisioned as a stand-alone film.<ref name="Deadline Kennedy" />

On [[June 17]], 2024, in another interview with ''Deadline'', Levy stated that production was slow-going, as it took time to develop a project with the amount of mythology and expanded universe that ''Star Wars'' has.<ref name="Deadline 2">{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/video/shawn-levy-video-interview-deadpool-and-wolverine|text=Shawn Levy Tells All: Working With Marvel, Directing 'Deadpool & Wolverine', His Dream 'Star Wars' Movie, And Navigating 'All The Light We Cannot See' And The Finale Of 'Stranger Things' – Behind The Lens|author=Pete Hammond|date=2024-06-17|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20240618210841}}</ref> On the premier for ''Deadpool & Wolverine'' on [[July 12]], Levy confirmed that [[Jonathan Tropper]] would be writing his ''Star Wars'' film and that Kennedy and Lucasfilm Chief Creative Officer [[Dave Filoni]] were excited on the premise.<ref name="ODE" /> On [[August 8]], Levy spoke with the Happy Sad Confused podcast where he was asked on the film. Levy stated that the experience of creating his ''Star Wars'' film has forced him to think on what ''Star Wars'' is as there were only so many times that ''Star Wars'' films could revisit the same part of the [[Timeline of galactic history|timeline]]. Levy commented that he's not interested in creating a redundant film, nor one where he has to serve another.<ref name="Collider" />

After rumors of plans that Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy was ready to retire, Kennedy provided an interview to ''Deadline'' to address the rumors and state of current ''Star Wars'' projects on [[February 27]], [[2025]]. Kennedy revealed that she is producing Shawn Levy's film following [[Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu|''The Mandalorian and Grogu'']], so would continue to remain at Lucasfilm. In terms of an official announcement, Kennedy stated that they were away from that for months to a year. During the interview with ''Deadline'', Kennedy also shared the setting of Levy's film, including that it may occur five to six years following the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']] and that characters from the [[sequel trilogy]] may appear. By the time of the interview, Levy had been working on his film for a year and a half.<ref name="KK Q&A" />

===Project achieves lift-off===
{{Quote|Shawn Levy just made the experience so pleasant for everybody, and we found this 14-year-old kid out of Ireland who had virtually no experience. That's always risky, hanging a story so much on a child actor. You’re not exactly sure how comfortable they’re going to be. Flynn Gray turned out to be such a special kid. ''[…]'' Not only was he there with Ryan Gosling; this movie is structured in a way that he had kind of a new actor coming in every few weeks that he was one-on-one with. Matt Smith, Amy Adams, Aaron Pierre. And each one, it was so great to watch him because he would just get so excited by the actors he got to work with. It was like he was in the best university you could possibly be in.|Kathleen Kennedy|<ref name="Deadline Kennedy" />}}
[[File:Star Wars Starfighter First image.png|thumb|left|250px|The first reveal from the set of ''Star Wars: Starfighter''.]]
On [[April 18]], [[2025]], the film was officially announced as ''Star Wars: Starfighter'' during [[Celebration Japan (2025)|Celebration Japan]] by [[Lucasfilm]], and revealed to begin production in the fall of 2025. During the announcement, it was revealed that [[Ryan Gosling]] was cast in the film, and was revealed to the audience on stage. The film is set to be released in theaters on [[May 28]], [[2027]].<ref name="Starfighter" /> Production of the film began in the [[Wikipedia:United Kingdom|United Kingdom]] on [[August 28]], 2025. That day, an article released on [[StarWars.com]] also revealed the principal cast of the film alongside the film's first released image, a black and white still of actors Gosling and [[Flynn Gray]] on set in front of a [[landspeeder]].<ref name="Cast Announcement" />

An [[Wikipedia:Instagram|Instagram]] post by Levy on [[September 17]] showed another still from the film and revealed that production also included scenes filmed in the [[Wikipedia:Mediterranean Sea|Mediterranean Sea]] at the coast of [[Wikipedia:Sardinia|Sardinia]], [[Wikipedia:Italy|Italy]].<ref name="Sardinia IG">{{Instagram|username=slevydirect|url=p/DOtlyDdDxnw|name=[[Shawn Levy]]|date=2025-09-17|quote=Somewhere in the Mediterranean Sea #Starfighter|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/sL9wz}}</ref>

A scene involving a [[lightsaber duel]] in a muddy pond was filmed in [[November]]. Levy invited actor [[Tom Cruise]], who was visiting the set at the time, to shoot some of the scene.<ref name="NYT Resuscitate">{{WebCite|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/08/movies/shawn-levy-star-wars-stranger-things.html|text=His Job Is to Resuscitate ‘Star Wars.’ No Pressure.|author=Calum Marsh|date=2026-01-08|work=[[Wikipedia:New York Times|New York Times]]|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/xtncF}}</ref>

==Release and reception==
[[File:Starfighter Water craft.png|thumb|right|250px|Ryan Gosling and Flynn Gray in the set of ''Star Wars: Starfighter'']]
On [[May 7]], [[2019]], [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]] revealed their future movie release schedule, including a set of three untitled ''Star Wars'' films, one of which had a scheduled release date of [[December 18]], [[2026]].<ref name="Variety Disney 2019">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2019/film/news/disney-avatar-star-wars-marvel-1203207661|text=Disney Moves 'Avatar' Sequels, Announces New 'Star Wars' Films|author=Brent Lang, Rebecca Rubin|date=2019-05-07|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20200727083136}}</ref> ''[[The Star Wars Show]]'' also reported on the news on [[May 15]].<ref name="SW Show">{{StarWarsShow|dUSoopV7EKo|Star Wars Dates Announced, Plus We Won an Emmy!|sw_url=video/star-wars-dates-announced-plus-we-won-an-emmy}}</ref> On [[July 23]], [[2020]], after the onset of the [[Wikipedia:COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19 pandemic]], the film was delayed to [[December 17]], 2027,<ref name="Variety 2020">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2020/film/box-office/star-wars-films-avatar-sequels-pushed-back-a-year-in-disney-release-calendar-shakeup-1234715104|text='Star Wars' Films, 'Avatar' Sequels Pushed Back a Year in Disney Release Calendar Shakeup|author=Rebecca Rubin|date=2020-07-23|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20200723212010}}</ref> where it remained as late as [[August 7]], 2024, where the release slot was mentioned in Disney's Q3 Earning's Presentation.<ref name="2024 Q3 Call">{{DisneyCompany|url=/app/uploads/2024/08/Q3-FY24-Earnings-Presentation.pdf|text=Q3 FY24 Earnings Presentation}}</ref>

''Starfighter'' was later announced as having a May 28, 2027 release date on April 18, 2025 at Celebration Japan,<ref name="Starfighter" /> and on [[May 22]], Disney released an updated film release schedule to the press, confirming that ''Starfighter'' had indeed taken the original December 2027 project slot, which had moved up to May, with the original December date now scheduled to be used by the [[Wikipedia:Marvel Studios|Marvel Studios]] film [[Wikipedia:Marvel Cinematic Universe: Phase Six#Avengers: Secret Wars (2027)|''Avengers: Secret Wars'']].<ref name="Deadline Avengers">{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2025/05/next-avengers-movies-push-release-dates-dog-stars-devil-wears-prada-1236409088|text=Disney Pushes Next Two 'Avengers' Movies; Dates 'The Dog Stars' & 'The Devil Wears Prada 2'|author=Matt Grobar|date=2025-05-22|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20250522230719}}</ref>
